story.title: Voters Participate in Six State Primaries Including Wisconsin and South Carolina
story.summary: Primary elections took place on August 11, 2026, in six states: Wisconsin, Minnesota, Alabama, Connecticut, Vermont, and South Carolina. Voters cast their ballots in key races, with notable outcomes in Wisconsin and South Carolina, where Trump-backed candidates experienced mixed results. Analysts provided insights into the implications of these elections for the upcoming political landscape.

explore_lenses.label: Is Wisconsin’s governor primary decided yet?
explore_lenses.title: No—delayed Milwaukee absentee results left it too close to call
explore_lenses.summary: As of August 12, the Democratic nomination for Wisconsin governor remained unresolved after a reporting error delayed roughly 28,000 Milwaukee absentee ballots.

claims.text: The contest between state Rep. Francesca Hong and Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley was still too early to call after Milwaukee officials said audit logs, rather than ballot results, had been uploaded to flash drives.
Crowley was endorsed by outgoing Democratic Gov. Tony Evers and presented himself as the more moderate candidate; Hong identifies as a democratic socialist.
If the final margin is under 1 percentage point, the losing candidate may seek a recount.
Wisconsin election-night totals are unofficial; municipal and county canvasses precede state certification.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in South Carolina’s Senate race?
explore_lenses.title: Graham and Norman move to an August 25 Republican runoff
explore_lenses.summary: The August 11 vote narrowed South Carolina’s special Republican Senate primary to Darline Graham and Ralph Norman; the runoff winner will become the party’s nominee for the November special election.

claims.text: Darline Graham and Ralph Norman emerged from a 10-candidate Republican field to advance to the August 25 runoff for the seat formerly held by Graham’s late brother, Sen. Lindsey Graham.

Graham credited Trump’s endorsement and said she would support his agenda; Norman’s campaign emphasized his congressional experience, while Democratic nominee Annie Andrews said her campaign would focus on affordability and health care.
AP forecast that the August 25 Republican runoff winner is expected to win the Senate seat over the Democratic nominee in the November special election.

The South Carolina Election Commission said voters who participated in the June Democratic primary could not vote in the August 11 special Republican primary, while June Republican-primary voters and voters who skipped both June primaries could participate.

story_report.summary: Voters cast ballots in primaries across Wisconsin, Minnesota, Alabama, Connecticut, Vermont and South Carolina on Aug. 11. Key races produced divergent results for candidates backed by President Donald Trump, while a Wisconsin Democratic contest remained unsettled because of a ballot-data handling problem. In South Carolina, Darline Graham and Ralph Norman advanced to a Republican Senate runoff scheduled for Aug. 25, setting up the next decision in a special-election race.

sections.heading: Wisconsin Democratic Contest Remains Uncalled
sections.body: The contest between state Rep. Francesca Hong and Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley was too early to call after Milwaukee officials said audit logs, rather than ballot results, were uploaded to flash drives. Crowley, endorsed by outgoing Democratic Gov. Tony Evers, presented himself as the more moderate candidate; Hong identifies as a democratic socialist. Election-night totals in Wisconsin remain unofficial pending municipal and county canvasses and state certification.

sections.heading: South Carolina Senate Runoff Approaches
sections.body: Graham and Norman emerged from a 10-candidate Republican field seeking the seat formerly held by Graham's late brother, Sen. Lindsey Graham. Graham credited Trump's endorsement and said she would support his agenda, while Norman emphasized his congressional experience; Democratic nominee Annie Andrews said she would focus on affordability and health care. The Associated Press forecast that the Republican runoff winner would be expected to defeat Andrews in November's special election.

sections.heading: South Carolina Primary Eligibility Rules
sections.body: South Carolina election officials said voters who participated in the June Democratic primary could not vote in the Aug. 11 special Republican primary. Those who voted in the June Republican primary, as well as voters who skipped both June primaries, were eligible to take part.

unresolved.text: Wisconsin's final vote total, any recount request and the certified nominee have not been established. If the final margin is below 1 percentage point, the losing candidate may seek a recount.
The results of the Aug. 25 South Carolina Republican runoff and the November special election remain unknown.

related_stories.title: David Crowley Wins Wisconsin Democratic Primary, Set to Face Tom Tiffany
related_stories.summary: David Crowley, the Milwaukee County executive, has won the Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor, defeating progressive candidate Francesca Hong. Crowley, who was backed by Governor Tony Evers, will face Republican Representative Tom Tiffany in the upcoming November election. This victory marks a notable shift in the Democratic primary landscape, as Crowley represents a more moderate stance compared to Hong's democratic socialist platform.

related_stories.title: Ferry Capsizes in Zimbabwe's Lake Kariba, Resulting in Multiple Fatalities and Missing Persons
related_stories.summary: A ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe, leading to at least 15 confirmed deaths and 27 individuals reported missing. Search and rescue operations are ongoing, with 77 people successfully rescued and taken to a nearby island. Authorities are coordinating efforts to bring the survivors back to safety.
